competitors.name: SignWell, Free Online Signature Maker (signwell.com/online-signature)
competitors.model: Free lead-magnet generator, no account. eSign free tier 3 documents/month with SignWell branding on every document and 5 active documents of storage; paid from $12/user/mo (Business $15/user/mo per aggregators)
competitors.note: The most dangerous competitor because it already makes our exact claim, in our exact words: 'we do not keep any record of your signature data or your signature image on our servers. Everything that happens related to your signature is done in your browser,' and 'Jump right in, no account or credit card needed.' Draw, type or upload; PNG and JPG out. It is polished, fast, and honest about the generator itself. The soft spot is the funnel underneath: the free generator exists to feed a $12 to 15/user/mo eSign product, so the page is ringed with CTAs, the free eSign tier stamps SignWell branding on your document, and recipients must create a free account to sign. It is also a venture-funded company that will always have a reason to eventually meter something, and it offers no vector output, no output-size control, and no guidance about when a generated signature is invalid.

competitors.name: Signaturely, Free Online Signature Generator (signaturely.com/online-signature)
competitors.model: Free generator behind an email capture; free eSign plan variously documented as 1 document/month (Signaturely's own page) or 3/month (third-party guides); paid tiers Personal/Business, with a live 'up to 35% off Business Plan' promo running when fetched
competitors.note: Ranks at or near the top for 'online signature generator' and offers both draw and type. Its privacy line is good and specific: 'Any signature created on this page through our signature generator is not saved on our servers. We won't save a record of your signature (or document) or share it with others.' The exploitable soft spot is the shape of the page, the signature block sits next to an email field and a 'Try for Free' button, and the footer CTA reads 'Sign 1 documents for free.' It is a marketing page with a tool embedded in it, not a tool. Its own pricing page and third-party pricing guides disagree about whether the free plan is 1 or 3 documents, which is itself a trust problem.

competitors.name: Adobe Acrobat (Reader Fill & Sign, plus the acrobat.com online sign-pdf tools)
competitors.model: Reader is free; the standalone Adobe Fill & Sign mobile app has been retired and no longer receives updates or support; the online tools require sign-in; Acrobat subscriptions run roughly $13 to 25/mo
competitors.note: Owns the trust halo, people search 'Adobe' when they do not know what else to use, and it is the tool your signature PNG will most often be dropped into. Two exploitable weaknesses. First, it is documented as degrading the very asset we produce: Adobe's own community thread 'Blurry signature image importing to Acrobat' records 'if I added a signature image in jpg or png format to the document using the Fill & Sign - Add Signature feature the image would be blurry. When adding the same file to the document using the Edit PDF - Add Image the signature image would be clear,' with a Community Expert replying 'Seems to me like a bug, since using the Select Image button from the Fill & Sign tool doesn't respect the bit depth of the selected image.' Second, Adobe retired the dedicated Fill & Sign app and pushed everyone into Acrobat Reader, and the online tools gate you behind an Adobe sign-in. So the default answer is now heavier, account-bound, and known to mangle signature images.

competitors.name: Apple Preview / iOS Markup (the real free competitor)
competitors.model: Free, pre-installed, no account; signatures persist and sync across Apple devices
competitors.note: This is the competitor that actually matters and the reason Mac users never search for this. Preview's Markup > Sign captures a signature three ways: trackpad, the built-in camera (hold your real pen-and-paper signature up to the lens against the blue line), or handoff to draw on an iPhone or iPad with a finger or Apple Pencil. The camera path is the best experience in the entire category because it is the only one that produces your actual signature rather than a mouse scrawl, and Apple then stores and reuses it. It also places the signature straight onto the PDF, which is the user's real goal. Two fatal gaps: it is Apple-only, Windows has no built-in equivalent at all, and it will not hand you a transparent PNG file you can use in Word, Google Docs, an email footer or a portal upload field. Our audience is Windows, ChromeOS, Android, and anyone on a locked-down work or library machine.

competitors.name: Docusign and Dropbox Sign (the eSign incumbents)
competitors.model: Docusign has no free plan, a 30-day trial, then Personal $15/mo capped at 5 envelopes/month, Standard $45, Business Pro $60. Dropbox Sign free tier is 3 signature requests/month; paid from $15/user/mo, Standard $25/user/mo (2-user minimum)
competitors.note: Not direct competitors for 'give me a PNG,' but they define what people think signing costs and they are where the search traffic ends up. Docusign's 2024 rebrand also fixed the category's visual language: Docusign Cobalt is the primary brand colour with Inkwell and Deep Violet secondary and Poppy red as accent, so cobalt-and-violet is now the incumbent look. The soft spot is enormous and structural: the overwhelming majority of the people typing 'signature maker' do not need an audit trail, a countersigner or an envelope, they need one image to drop into one document once. The whole category sells enterprise workflow to a person filling in a rental application, then charges $15/month for the privilege.

competitors.name: Online PNG Tools / Browserling (onlinepngtools.com/transparent-png-signature-maker)
competitors.model: Genuinely client-side but metered: free plan is personal use only, with limited daily usage, a wait timer on downloads, and ads; premium unlocks commercial use, unlimited use, instant download, no ads and clipboard copy
competitors.note: Technically excellent and technically honest, it states 'All conversions and calculations are done in your browser using JavaScript. We don't send a single bit about your input data to our servers,' and offers paper-colour thresholding, outline smoothing and an opacity mask so you can see exactly what became transparent. Those knockout controls are better than anything we have. The soft spot is that it proves client-side does not mean free: it still runs ads, still counts your uses, still puts a deliberate wait timer between you and your own file, and still reserves copy-to-clipboard for paying users. That is a paywall on a computation that costs the operator nothing, and it is the single most quotable piece of evidence that the metering in this category is a business decision rather than a cost.

competitors.name: The client-side clone swarm (serverless.tools, hcodx, textstudio, signaturegen.ai, DocHub SVG generator, pixmuse, portimg, signaturesketch.tech, signature.imageonline.co, mysignature.io)
competitors.model: Free, no signup, monetisation usually unstated (SEO, ads, or funnel into a paid parent product)
competitors.note: Our actual competitive set, and the reason positioning is hard. 'Free, no signup, 100% client-side, transparent PNG' is now boilerplate that a dozen near-identical sites assert on page one. Several are genuinely good and already beat us on features: serverless.tools ships 16 handwriting fonts and exports PNG and SVG entirely client-side; hcodx advertises 31 handwriting fonts; textstudio produces true vector output; DocHub gives away an SVG signature generator; signaturegen.ai uses sequence-to-sequence handwriting modelling for pen flourishes and animation. So they have vector export and typed signatures and we have neither. The claim is free to make, so the claim no longer differentiates, proof, judgement and craft do.

competitors.name: The exam-form signature resizer vertical (signatureresizer.com, photocopywala, examformtools, readytosubmit, utiltap, resizer.exammint)
competitors.model: Free, ad-supported, mostly Indian market, built entirely around one bureaucratic constraint
competitors.note: An entire cottage industry that exists because government application portals reject signature files on exact specifications, and it is invisible from the US-centric view of this category. Published requirements: UPSC 3.5 x 1.5 cm at up to 300 KB, SSC 30 KB, IBPS 140 x 60 px at 30 KB, SBI 160 x 60 px, RBI 140 x 60 px, RRB 100 KB, NEET UG and JEE Main 30 KB, every one of them JPG, white background, black ink. Rejection causes, in the order these guides list them: capital letters instead of running hand, wrong file size, coloured background, printed or typed appearance, wrong dimensions, and 'Format not JPEG, PNG is commonly rejected.' The soft spot is quality: these are ad-heavy, upload-based, single-purpose pages. The opportunity is that our app exports the one format these portals reject, and nobody in the well-designed tier of this category has noticed this workflow exists.

competitors.name: App-store signature apps, and Artlogo at the bespoke end
competitors.model: Store apps: free download, ads on nearly every interaction, subscriptions and IAP. Artlogo: hand-drawn calligraphy signature packages roughly $39-$119+; Fiverr signature-logo services around $140 to 160; independent calligraphers $75 to 350
competitors.note: Two ends of the same market. The store apps are where the category's reputation was destroyed: review summaries for the leading 'Signature Maker' and 'Watermark Maker: Add Signature' listings describe ads within a second of launch, a new ad on every tap, 'try premium' popups covering the signature you are trying to look at, an inability to save output outside the app without paying, and users reporting charges for an app they downloaded free and never opened. Artlogo is the opposite failure: a genuinely beautiful, genuinely expensive artefact aimed at people who want a signature as a personal brand mark. Neither serves the actual median user, who has a PDF open in another tab and eleven minutes.

complaints.complaint: A software-generated signature can now cost you your application and your filing fee. USCIS does not accept 'signatures typed on a keyboard, stamped, generated by software, or signed by an attorney on behalf of the applicant,' and also rejects digital signature images copied and pasted from other documents and signatures created by auto-pen or signature software. What changed: DHS published the interim final rule 'Signatures on Immigration Benefit Requests' in the Federal Register on 11 May 2026, effective 10 July 2026, amending 8 CFR 103.2(a)(7)(ii)(A) so adjudicators may reject OR DENY a filing later found to lack a valid signature even after it cleared the Lockbox, retaining the fee, treating the case as adjudicated, and allowing no post-filing correction. Signature-related denials rose from 300 in FY2021 to 2,953 in FY2025.
complaints.source: federalregister.gov/documents/2026/05/11/2026-09289 (Signatures on Immigration Benefit Requests); citizenpath.com/uscis-signature-requirements quoting USCIS's own definition; corroborating analyses from Mintz (insight 2806), Ogletree, Erickson Immigration Group, Reddy Neumann Brown and AILA
complaints.weWinIf: We become the only tool in the category honest enough to tell you not to use it. A short, permanent 'Where this works, and where it does not' block: fine for a rental agreement, a school form, a vendor invoice, an email footer; NOT for USCIS forms, wills, adoption papers or court orders, where a wet signature is required. For those, give the correct three-step route (print, sign in ink, scan) and hand off to our own scan-to-pdf app. Every competitor's incentive is to get you to sign; ours is not, and this is the single most valuable thing that asymmetry buys us, especially in the first months after a rule that forfeits fees.

complaints.complaint: PNG is the wrong format for the highest-volume signature-upload workflow on earth, and the specs are unforgiving. Government exam portals demand JPG on a white background at exact dimensions and byte sizes, IBPS and RBI 140 x 60 px at 30 KB, SBI 160 x 60 px, SSC 3.5 x 1.5 cm at 30 KB, UPSC up to 300 KB, RRB 100 KB, and the published rejection list includes 'Format not JPEG, PNG is commonly rejected,' 'Coloured background instead of white,' 'Wrong file size (above limit or too low/blurry),' and 'Capital letters used, signatures on Indian exam forms must be in cursive/running handwriting.' Guides warn that even a minor discrepancy in pixel dimensions, aspect ratio, file size or format causes instant rejection.
complaints.source: examformtools.in/blog/signature-specifications-indian-competitive-exams-complete-guide (full per-exam spec table and ranked rejection reasons); readytosubmit.in/tools/signature-size-checker; photocopywala.in/tools/signature-resizer; resizer.exammint.in/signature-resizer
complaints.weWinIf: Add an export panel with a live readout, output dimensions in px and the resulting file size in KB, shown BEFORE the download, plus named presets that hit the real thresholds (140x60 JPG 30 KB, 160x60, 3.5x1.5 cm, plus a free-size transparent PNG for documents). A quality slider that targets a KB ceiling rather than a percentage. This is a handful of lines of canvas code and it converts our app from a nice-looking toy into the only well-designed tool that clears a real bureaucratic gate.

complaints.complaint: The white box. A signature saved as a JPG or a photographed scrap of paper arrives as an opaque rectangle that covers the text underneath it, and the workarounds people are taught are miserable, Word's Background Removal tool, or 'pick Brightness and select a 30% or 40% brightness level... 50% sharpness, increasing brightness by +40%, and reducing contrast by -40%.' A whole tier of tools (remove.bg's dedicated signature-background page, signatureresizer's background remover, insMind, fococlipping) exists purely to undo this.
complaints.source: dignited.com/34810/remove-signature-background-using-microsoft-word; remove.bg/f/remove-signature-background; signatureresizer.com/signature-background-remover; insmind.com and fococlipping how-to guides
complaints.weWinIf: We already solve this, app.js crops to the ink with a tested trimBounds and exports a transparent PNG, but we never SHOW it. Put the output on a checkerboard preview at actual export size, over a sample line of body text, so the transparency is visible before download rather than asserted in a hint paragraph. Then offer the white-background JPG variant explicitly for the portals that require it, labelled with why. Proving transparency is worth more than claiming it.

complaints.complaint: The signature you place comes out blurry, jagged or discoloured, and the market leader has a documented bug doing exactly that. Adobe Community: 'the problem was that if I added a signature image in jpg or png format to the document using the Fill & Sign - Add Signature feature the image would be blurry. When adding the same file to the document using the Edit PDF - Add Image the signature image would be clear.' And: 'When I insert the signature as a regular image it renders fine. When I insert the image using the Add Signature function, it renders with a grey board and the color changes.' A Community Expert responded: 'the Fill & Sign tool seems to be buggy since it appears that it was not designed with the idea in mind to expand and maintain a non-blurred aspect ratio.'
complaints.source: community.adobe.com/t5/acrobat-discussions/blurry-signature-image-importing-to-acrobat/m-p/12364521 (thread also indexed as community question 1263068); community.adobe.com question 1304076 'Signature image appears blurry and discolored'
complaints.weWinIf: Export generously and say so. We already render at 3x, but the user has no idea what they are getting: state the output dimensions and the effective print size on the button ('1840 x 520 px, about 6 inches wide at 300 dpi'). Offer a 'for printing' preset that guarantees 300 dpi at a stated physical width. Since the receiving tool may downsample, giving people more pixels than they think they need is the only defence we control.

complaints.complaint: Drawing with a mouse or trackpad produces something that looks nothing like your signature. This is the category's founding problem: competitors' own copy recommends buying a stylus, macOS Preview added camera capture specifically to escape it, and the standard open-source canvas (szimek/signature_pad, 'variable width Bézier curve interpolation based on Smoother Signatures post by Square') exists because a constant-width line reads as a doodle. Stroke width there is derived from the distance between sampled points as a proxy for velocity, so fast strokes thin out and slow ones thicken.
complaints.source: github.com/szimek/signature_pad and npmjs.com/package/signature_pad (variable-width Bézier, velocity filter weight, min/max line width); support.apple.com/guide/preview/prvw35725 (camera and iPhone capture); competitor copy on signaturely.com/online-signature/draw and mysignature.io recommending a stylus
complaints.weWinIf: Two fixes, both cheap because we already keep the geometry. (1) Vary stroke width by pointer velocity, and use ev.pressure, which our pointermove handler already receives and throws away, when a stylus reports it. This is the single change that makes a drawn signature look drawn. (2) Give people the escape hatch Apple has and the web does not: import a photo of a signature written with a real pen on real paper, and knock the paper out client-side with a visible threshold control. The best signature is still the one made with a pen.

complaints.complaint: Signature canvases break on phones in ways that make people give up. 'On mobile phones, after you draw your signature and scroll down a little, if you go back up, it vanishes from the canvas. The data is still there, but the signature goes missing.' A parallel issue is titled 'Canvas Clears when scrolling on iPad.' And the more basic failure: the page scrolls instead of drawing, with users told to work around it by zooming until the signature box fills the screen or switching the browser to Desktop mode.
complaints.source: github.com/szimek/signature_pad issue 254 'Signature on Mobile Device Missing on Scroll'; github.com/thread-pond/signature-pad issue 156 'Canvas Clears when scrolling on iPad'; laptopjudge.com/touch-screen-scrolls-instead-of-draws-in-signature-box
complaints.weWinIf: We already avoid the worst of this, touch-action:none on .padwrap and a redraw from stored points on resize, but we do not go far enough. The pad is a fixed 260px band inside a 40rem column, which on a phone in portrait is a letterbox roughly a finger and a half tall. Add a full-bleed 'Sign big' mode that takes the whole viewport in landscape, and rescale stored strokes proportionally on rotation instead of leaving them in absolute CSS pixels, so a portrait signature is not clipped by a landscape crop. Signing large is also the advice our own hint already gives, the UI should make it possible instead of just recommending it.

complaints.complaint: Client-side is not the same as free. Online PNG Tools states plainly 'All conversions and calculations are done in your browser using JavaScript. We don't send a single bit about your input data to our servers', and then meters the free plan to personal use only, limited daily attempts, ads, a deliberate wait timer before you can download, and copy-to-clipboard reserved for premium. Nothing about that computation costs the operator anything.
complaints.weWinIf: Say the quiet part exactly where they put their pricing table: no counter, no wait timer, no personal-use-only licence, no premium clipboard. Add copy-to-clipboard as a first-class button next to download, precisely because a competitor charges for it, it is the fastest path into Google Docs, Word and an email footer, and it costs us a ClipboardItem call.

complaints.complaint: The free generator that turns out to be an email wall or a document counter. Signaturely's generator page puts an email field and a 'Try for Free' button next to the signature block, and its footer CTA reads 'Sign 1 documents for free' while third-party pricing guides claim 3, the tool's own sources disagree. SignWell's free eSign tier is 3 documents/month, stamps SignWell branding on every document sent, caps storage at 5 active documents, and requires recipients to create a free account to sign.
complaints.source: signaturely.com/online-signature/ and signaturely.com/pricing; signwell.com/electronic-signature; verdocs.com/signwell-pricing and verdocs.com/signaturely-pricing; esign.ai/blog/signwell-free-plan-limitations-and-features
complaints.weWinIf: Zero interstitial between 'done' and the file in Downloads: no email, no modal, no rating prompt, no tip prompt anywhere on the export path. The tip link stays a link in the header and footer, never a button on the critical path. And show the output filename and size next to the download control before it is pressed, so it is visibly obvious there is nothing left to happen.

complaints.complaint: Store signature apps are ad-saturated to the point of unusability, and some bill people who never opened them. Review summaries for the leading listings describe ads within a second of launch and a fresh ad on every single tap; 'try premium' popups appearing on every style selection and covering the signature itself so you cannot see what you made; saved signatures unusable without a subscription; PDFs that cannot be saved outside the app without paying; and users reporting charges on a free download they never opened.
complaints.source: Google Play and App Store listings for 'Signature Maker: Digital Sign' (com.signaturemaker.app), 'Signature Maker: Sign Creator', 'Electronic Signature Maker' (com.cpctech.signaturemakerpro) and 'Watermark Maker: Add Signature' (id1160624432), surfaced via search-result summaries. CAVEAT: both stores render reviews with JavaScript and I could not fetch the review text directly, so these are paraphrases of aggregated review summaries, not verbatim quotes I read on the page.
complaints.weWinIf: Be installable and offline as a PWA so there is no store, no SDK, no ad slot and no billing surface at all, and make that a stated fact on the page, not a feature bullet. Nothing may ever appear over the signing pad or the export button: no banner, no toast that covers the canvas, nothing in the thumb zone that moves or grows.

complaints.complaint: Your signature image is the most reusable credential you own, and once it is out you cannot revoke it. A 2025 academic paper exists specifically on this: 'AuthSig: Safeguarding Scanned Signatures Against Unauthorized Reuse in Paperless Workflows.' Practitioner sources put it bluntly, scanned signatures are static images that can be copied, altered or reused without the signer's consent, and fraudsters scan real signatures and modify them to fit different documents, showing up in electronic contracts, falsified tax documents and corporate fraud. The Identity Theft Resource Center has issued a public advisory about e-signature phishing scams.
complaints.source: arxiv.org/pdf/2511.08967 (AuthSig, Nov 2025); idtheftcenter.org post 'Have You Received a Suspicious Email Asking for a Signature? It Could Be an E-Signature Scam'; ge-sign.com and certinal.com practitioner guides on scanned-signature reuse
complaints.weWinIf: Take a real position instead of a reassuring one. Default to storing nothing, which is already true in our build, but say so as a deliberate choice with a reason, not as an absent feature: 'This app never keeps your signature. Close the tab and it is gone. That is on purpose.' If we later add save-for-next-time, it must be opt-in, local-only, and paired with a one-tap wipe. And add a short, unpatronising line about handling the file afterwards: it is as sensitive as a scan of your passport.

complaints.complaint: There is no way to make a signature without a working pointing device, which is an ADA and Section 508 problem, not a nice-to-have. Accessibility guidance is consistent: drawing poses challenges for users with motor impairments, so platforms include typing as an alternative to comply with the ADA; users with limited motor skills often cannot use a mouse and rely on a keyboard or switch device, so every interactive element must be reachable with Tab and Enter; uploading an image of a handwritten signature is the other accessible route, provided the control is labelled. Section508.gov additionally requires that a signature within a scanned document be marked as a figure with equivalent alternative text.
complaints.source: section508.gov/create/electronic-signatures; techplayon.com 'Accessibility Standards in Electronic Signature Platforms'; accessibility.com 'Accessibility Features Of Docusign'; accessabilityofficer.com on accessible digital signatures for blind users; esign.ai/blog/draw-vs-type-signature-options
complaints.weWinIf: This is the strongest argument for the typed path we do not have, and it reframes it from a nice extra to a requirement. Ship type-a-signature with real handwriting faces, plus photo import, plus a drawn canvas, three routes to the same output, all keyboard-reachable, and give the canvas an accessible name and a described alternative rather than leaving a bare element. The portfolio just ran an accessibility verify round; this app is the one where the primary interaction is still pointer-only.

complaints.complaint: Ink colour is a real requirement that nobody explains. Black signatures are indistinguishable from a black-and-white photocopy, which is an opening for fraud; blue makes an original visually distinct from a copy. For mortgage closings and other financial signings, blue ink is described as not just preferred but functionally required by most lenders and title companies, and some countries mandate blue for the same reason. Meanwhile exam portals mandate the opposite, black ink on white.
complaints.source: legalclarity.org 'Should You Sign in Blue or Black Ink?' and 'What Color Ink Should a Notary Sign In'; notarystyle.com and thenotaryeducationgrp.com on blue-vs-black for signing agents; examformtools.in spec table (black ink, white background)
complaints.weWinIf: We already ship exactly two inks, black #111318 and blue #1d3f8f, and say nothing about either. Attach the reason to the swatch in one line each: black for scanning, printing and exam portals; blue because it proves the document is an original and not a photocopy, which lenders and title companies expect. This is free, it is true, and it makes a two-button colour picker feel like expertise instead of a limitation.

complaints.complaint: A typed script-font signature is legally valid in ordinary commerce but quietly wrong in several places people actually use it. ESIGN and UETA give a typed name the same weight as ink when intent, consent, attribution and a reliable record are present, but wills, adoption papers and court orders are carved out, USCIS rejects typed and script-font signatures outright, and regulatory reviewers 'sometimes prefer plain, standard fonts because unusual typefaces can raise questions about tampering.' Every generator in the category leads with typed script signatures and none of them mentions any of this.
complaints.source: juro.com/learn/esign-act-ueta; agrello.io/articles/typed-signature-legal; resources.signnow.com/info-esignature/what-font-to-use-for-electronic-signature; immigration-analytics.com on USCIS digital signature rules; citizenpath.com/uscis-signature-requirements
complaints.weWinIf: Ship the typed path, then be the only one that qualifies it, one plain sentence under the font picker naming where a typed signature is fine and where it is not, and linking the drawn or wet-ink route for the exceptions. Competitors will not copy this because a caveat reduces their conversion rate; for us it is the whole reputation.

tableStakes: Type-a-signature with real handwriting faces, as an equal-status route alongside drawing. VERIFIED GAP: /workspaces/SWS-apps/apps/signature-maker/index.html contains only <canvas id="pad"> and a draw toolbar; the sole @font-face is Fraunces (the portfolio's display serif for headings) and /workspaces/SWS-apps/apps/signature-maker/fonts/ contains only fraunces-latin.woff2. There is no typed path at all, even though the portfolio brief describes this app as 'draw or type.' SignWell, Signaturely, serverless.tools (16 fonts) and hcodx (31 fonts) all have it, and accessibility guidance treats typing as the required alternative to drawing.

Import a photo or scan of a real pen-and-paper signature and knock out the paper, with a visible threshold control. VERIFIED GAP: no file input, no drop target and no image decode anywhere in index.html or /workspaces/SWS-apps/apps/signature-maker/app.js. macOS Preview's camera capture and Online PNG Tools' threshold-plus-opacity-mask are both better than anything we offer, and this is the only route that produces a signature that actually looks like the user's.

Vector (SVG) export. VERIFIED GAP: app.js download() ends at out.toDataURL('image/png'), PNG is the only output. We already retain full stroke geometry in the strokes array as point lists, and helpers.js already exports smoothSegments() returning quadratic segments, so an SVG path is almost free. DocHub, textstudio, serverless.tools and signaturegen.ai all ship SVG.

JPEG on a white background as an alternative export. VERIFIED GAP: same single toDataURL('image/png') call. Every Indian exam portal, the highest-volume signature-upload workflow in the world, requires JPG on white and commonly rejects PNG outright.

Control over output dimensions and file size, with the numbers shown before download. VERIFIED GAP: app.js hardcodes const SCALE = 3 over a fixed 260px-tall pad and reads pad.clientWidth at click time; there is no width, height, dpi or KB control and no readout of what you are about to get. Portals enforce 140x60 px and 30 KB; print needs 300 dpi. Right now the output size is an accident of the browser window.

Copy to clipboard. VERIFIED GAP: download() only builds an <a download> and clicks it. Clipboard is the fastest route into Google Docs, Word and an email footer, and Online PNG Tools charges money for it, which tells you how much people want it.

Undo AND redo, with the controls disabled when there is nothing to do. PARTIAL GAP: app.js wires undoBtn to strokes.pop() with no redo stack, and neither undoBtn nor clearBtn is ever disabled. Clear wipes everything with no confirmation and no way back, on the one artefact the user cannot easily reproduce.

Variable stroke width driven by speed or stylus pressure. VERIFIED GAP: drawStroke() sets ctx.lineWidth = s.size * DPR, a constant for the whole stroke, and the pointermove handler calls getCoalescedEvents() but stores only {x, y}, ev.pressure is received and discarded. Constant-width strokes are the reason a mouse signature reads as a doodle; szimek/signature_pad has done velocity-based variable-width Bézier for a decade.

Matching initials generated alongside the signature. VERIFIED GAP: not present in index.html or app.js. Every eSign product produces an initials mark because contracts ask you to initial pages, and a user who has to come back and draw a second, smaller mark has been sent away mid-task.

A keyboard- and assistive-technology-reachable way to produce a signature. VERIFIED GAP: the pad is <canvas id="pad"></canvas> with no tabindex, no role, no aria-label and no fallback content, and drawing is the only route to an output, so a person using a keyboard, a switch device or a screen reader cannot make a signature at all. Section 508 guidance and ADA practice both name typing and image upload as the required alternatives.

A visible, on-page privacy statement rendered as an object rather than a sentence. PARTIAL GAP: the .trust component is defined in this app's own CSS (index.html around line 437, including a print override at line 1227) but never instantiated in the body, the promise appears only as a hero sentence and a grey footer line. Across the whole portfolio only /workspaces/SWS-apps/apps/pill-schedule/index.html actually uses class="trust". In the app where privacy IS the product, the studio's own trust stamp is sitting unused in the stylesheet.

Works fully offline as an installable PWA with no account, no ads, no watermark and no export gate. WE HAVE THIS: sw.js (VERSION sig-v14) precaches every asset including the font and claims clients; manifest.webmanifest is standalone-display; firebase.json sets a strict default-src 'self' CSP with object-src 'none' and frame-ancestors 'none'; the tip link is a header/footer link, never on the export path. Palm rejection is handled properly too, app.js tracks a single activePointer so a resting hand cannot zigzag the stroke, which is more care than most competitors take.
differentiators: Be the only signature tool that tells you when not to use it. A permanent 'Where this works, and where it does not' block: fine for leases, school forms, vendor paperwork and email footers; not for USCIS filings, wills, adoption papers or court orders. This is urgent rather than academic, the DHS interim final rule effective 10 July 2026 lets USCIS deny a filing for an invalid signature after intake and keep the fee, with no post-filing correction, and signature denials already went from 300 in FY2021 to 2,953 in FY2025. Every competitor's incentive is to make you sign; ours is not. Pair the warning with the correct route (print, sign in ink, scan) and hand off to our own scan-to-pdf app.

Make the privacy claim falsifiable rather than asserted, because SignWell already makes our exact claim in our exact words and the clone swarm makes it as boilerplate. A line the user can act on in five seconds, 'Turn your Wi-Fi off. It still works.', backed by a genuinely offline PWA, a single-origin CSP already enforced in firebase.json, a named studio with a real privacy page, and a link to the source. In a category where the artefact is the most forgeable thing a person owns, verifiability beats adjectives.

Make a drawn signature actually look drawn. Velocity-derived stroke width plus stylus pressure (ev.pressure is already arriving in our pointermove handler and being thrown away), and a full-bleed landscape 'Sign big' sheet on phones instead of the current 260px letterbox. Our own hint already tells people to 'sign larger than feels natural', the interface should make that possible rather than merely advise it.

Bring Apple's best idea to everyone else: photograph your real pen-and-paper signature and knock out the paper, entirely client-side, with a visible threshold slider and a before/after. Preview's camera capture is the best experience in the category and it is Mac-only; Windows has no equivalent at all. This also quietly solves the accessibility case, someone who cannot draw with a mouse can still sign with a pen and photograph it.

Own the export nobody else designs for: a live px and KB readout before download, with named presets for the gates that actually reject people, 140x60 JPG at 30 KB for IBPS and RBI, 160x60 for SBI, 3.5x1.5 cm for SSC and UPSC, plus a transparent PNG for documents and a 300 dpi print size stated in inches. The resizer vertical serves this need with ads and uploads; nobody in the well-designed tier serves it at all.

Emit vector. We already hold the stroke geometry and helpers.js already computes smoothed quadratic segments, so an SVG path costs almost nothing and gives us the one output that never pixelates in the tool the user pastes into, which matters because Adobe's own Fill & Sign is documented blurring raster signatures.

Attach the reason to every choice. Black for scanning, printing and exam portals; blue because it proves an original against a photocopy, which lenders and title companies expect. One clause per swatch turns a two-colour picker into visible expertise, and no competitor does it because their pages are optimised for conversion, not comprehension.

Take a stated position on storage rather than having no feature. 'This app never keeps your signature, close the tab and it is gone. That is on purpose,' with any future save being opt-in, local-only and paired with a one-tap wipe. The account-based competitors structurally cannot say this, and for an asset that can be reused against you indefinitely it is the correct posture, not merely a cheap one.

Finish the job instead of handing over a PNG. The user's goal is a signed document, not an image file. A 'place it on a PDF' handoff into our own pdf-tools, and a 'sign on your phone, use on your laptop' path, close the gap that makes people go back to Adobe. Nobody else in the free-generator tier owns the next step, and we already own both apps.

aesthetic.categoryConventions: The category splits into three visual dialects and all three are exploitable. First, the eSign incumbents: since Docusign's 2024 rebrand the house style is Docusign Cobalt as primary with Inkwell and Deep Violet secondary and Poppy red as a sparing accent, deployed as bright gradients over enterprise-clean layouts, cobalt-and-violet now reads as 'the signing category' the way red reads as 'the PDF category.' Second, the SEO generator tier: a marketing landing page with an H1, a screenshot, a wall of handwriting-font specimens, a testimonial strip and a comparison table, with the actual signing canvas pushed below the fold and ringed by CTAs; the tell is that the tool is an embed inside an advertisement. Third, the ornamental tier, Artlogo, calligraphy sellers, Fancy Signature Maker apps, which reaches for parchment textures, gold foil, quill pens, wax seals and swashy display type, selling a signature as a personal luxury brand mark. Dated tells across all three: skeuomorphic paper curl and drop shadows, gradient buttons, a fake ballpoint or quill cursor, animated 'writing' hero loops, cookie banners, a font-specimen grid rendering the same three words thirty-one times, and the interstitial between finishing and downloading. What reads as current in 2026: the working surface visible immediately with no landing preamble, near-flat high-contrast neutral surfaces, exactly one accent used for state rather than decoration, generous whitespace, real dark-mode support, and accessibility-first defaults. And one hard constraint specific to this app that overrides fashion: the signing pad must be a true white rectangle in every theme, because it is a WYSIWYG preview of ink on a document, a tinted or dark-mode-inverted pad turns the exported ink colour into a guess. Our build already hardcodes .padwrap to #ffffff, and that should be defended in any redesign, not tidied into a token.
aesthetic.emotionalContext: Nobody opens this for fun and nobody opens it twice in a row. The trigger is a document already open in another tab with a signature-shaped hole in it: a lease, an offer letter, a school permission form, a W-9, a vendor invoice, an exam application closing tonight, a parent's insurance claim being handled by the family's designated computer person. The user is mid-task, on a deadline, and on whatever machine they happen to have, frequently Windows or a Chromebook, frequently a work or library machine where nothing can be installed, which is precisely why they are in a browser and not in Preview. There is a specific and unusual emotional charge here that other utilities do not carry: this is the one file in the portfolio that can be used against you. People know a signature image is forgeable, they have been told not to email pictures of it, and a tool asking them to draw it on a website they found in a search result is being asked for a lot of trust in about four seconds. That distrust is heightened right now by the FBI's 2025 advisory about malicious free document tools and by the flood of near-identical signature sites, which means looking generic is itself a risk signal. Practically this dictates: the pad on screen with no scrolling and no preamble; the privacy promise as a visible object at the top of the surface rather than grey text at the bottom; the export path with nothing between the button and the file; large enough targets and a signing area big enough to actually sign in on a 390px phone; and no cheerfulness, no confetti, no 'Nice signature!', no animated flourish. Someone signing a medical release or a redundancy acknowledgement does not want the app to be pleased. Also assume the user is slightly embarrassed by how their mouse signature looks, and will draw it four or five times: undo, clear and redraw must be immediate and unjudgemental, and the third attempt must be as fast as the first. The register is a good stationer or a notary's desk: exact, discreet, unhurried, competent, and completely uninterested in your attention.
aesthetic.recommendedFeel: discreet, exact, unhurried, ink-on-paper, notarial, restrained, trustworthy

colorRecommendation.hueFamily: Keep the near-achromatic ink concept but make it a true blue-black rather than a grey: hue held around 266 to 270 with chroma raised from 0.022 to roughly 0.05 to 0.06 and the accent lightness driven down to a genuine ink value (OKLCH L around 0.26 to 0.30, near #1b1f36 to #232842), on the existing warm paper ground. Crucially, the accent should BE the pen: the default ink swatch, the primary button fill and the focus ring should all be the same blue-black, so the brand colour is literally the colour of the thing the user is making. Keep the second swatch as the documents blue (#1d3f8f) and add its justification. Reserve one warm rust or amber tone strictly for the 'this form needs a wet signature' warning, never for buttons, never decoratively.
colorRecommendation.rationale: Three forces decide this. (1) PORTFOLIO, there is a real collision in skins.mjs that a redesign must fix. signature-maker is currently hue 264 / chroma 0.022 / warm paper / editorial voice / grain texture, and caregiver-log is hue 250 / chroma 0.035 / warm paper / editorial voice / grain texture. Fourteen degrees apart, both near-achromatic, and identical on all four remaining axes: these are effectively the same skin, and caregiver-log's note explicitly claims the quiet-neutral position ('near-neutral slate on linen, quiet on purpose'). Two apps cannot both be the quiet one. The way out is value and chroma, not hue, because at 23 apps the wheel is packed at roughly 15-degree intervals and there is no empty band left: the blue-violet arc runs bill-splitter 218, pill-schedule 234, caregiver-log 250, team-parent 258, signature-maker 264, pdf-tools 276, baby-log 294. Holding 266 to 270 keeps us clear of team-parent (258, cool paper, technical voice, band texture) and pdf-tools (276, cool paper, technical voice, no texture), the paper and voice axes already separate us decisively from both, while dropping the accent to near-black at low chroma separates us from caregiver-log's mid-value slate by value, which is the strongest separator available and the one the skin system explicitly recommends when hue is crowded. I would also swap texture from 'grain' to 'rule': it is already in the fixed vocabulary, it is currently used only by sub-plans at hue 174 so there is no visual collision, and a feint baseline rule is semantically the signature line, the app already draws one as .padline. (2) CATEGORY, since Docusign's 2024 rebrand the incumbent palette is Docusign Cobalt primary with Inkwell and Deep Violet secondary and a Poppy red accent, so mid-value cobalt and saturated violet now read as 'generic eSign SaaS,' and Adobe owns red outright next door in the PDF tools we sit beside. A near-black ink is the one value the category does not use for chrome, because every competitor reserves black for the signature itself and paints the UI in brand colour. Making the UI the same colour as the ink is a genuine, cheap, defensible inversion. (3) FUNCTION, which is the deciding argument, the subject of this screen is a dark mark on a white rectangle. Any chromatic UI accent competes with the artefact, which is exactly why the existing skin note ('the app is ink on paper; anything else competes with the thing the user is drawing') is correct and should be kept. But near-achromatic at chroma 0.022 is currently so timid that the app has no identity at all, and the two ink swatches it does ship (#111318 and #1d3f8f) are hardcoded in the markup and belong to no palette. Binding the accent to the pen fixes both problems at once: the app gains a colour, and the colour is honest. Also keep the pad hardcoded white in both themes and keep the warm cream canvas, white paper on cream reads as a sheet on a desk and gives the signing area free structure, whereas a cool grey-white ground would let it float.
colorRecommendation.avoid: Cobalt and deep violet in any brand role, Docusign's post-2024 palette is built on exactly those two, and team-parent (258 / 0.15) and pdf-tools (276 / 0.135) already hold those slots in this portfolio. Raising chroma at hue 264 into the mid range for the same reason: it walks straight into both neighbours. Mid-value desaturated slate at low chroma, that is caregiver-log (250 / 0.035 / warm / editorial / grain), and shipping a second one makes two apps indistinguishable in a hub grid. Adobe red and Docusign's Poppy accent, this app will be seen next to pdf-tools and scan-to-pdf, and red is the category's counterfeit signal. Gold, amber or brass as a brand hue, signup-sheets (58 / 0.155), bracket-maker (104 / 0.14) and moving-boxes (72 / 0.105) already occupy that band, and gold also drags the page toward the Artlogo calligraphy register, which is the wrong promise for someone filling in a rental application. Green as a 'secure / verified' chrome colour, qr-maker (142), grocery-list (158) and home-inventory (124) hold green, and a padlock-green trust badge is exactly the boilerplate the clone swarm uses. Pure #000 as the default pen: no real pen is pure black, and the existing #111318 is correct, do not simplify it. Any dark-mode treatment that inverts, tints or darkens the signing pad: the pad is a preview of ink on white paper, so a dark pad makes the exported colour a lie; in dark mode the pad stays white and the surrounding chrome darkens around it. Skeuomorphic parchment, wax seals, quill or fountain-pen imagery, gold foil and swash display type, that is the ornamental tier's costume and it undermines the notarial register the emotional context calls for. And never let colour alone carry the 'this signature will be rejected' warning: it needs an icon, a label and plain words, because the cost of missing it is now a forfeited USCIS filing fee.

confidence: MEDIUM-HIGH overall. HIGHEST CONFIDENCE OF ALL, the gaps in our own build, which I verified by reading /workspaces/SWS-apps/apps/signature-maker/index.html, app.js, helpers.js, sw.js and manifest.webmanifest directly, plus /workspaces/SWS-apps/design/skins.mjs and /workspaces/SWS-apps/firebase.json. Verified facts, not inference: PNG is the only export (a single out.toDataURL('image/png') in download()); SCALE is hardcoded to 3 over a fixed 260px pad; there is no typed path, no image import, no clipboard, no redo, no persistence, no initials and no output-size control; drawStroke uses a constant ctx.lineWidth and the pointermove handler receives ev.pressure and discards it; the canvas element has no tabindex, role, aria-label or fallback content; the .trust component is defined in this app's CSS (index.html ~line 437) but never used in its body, and pill-schedule is the only app in the portfolio that instantiates it; the app IS a real offline PWA (sw.js sig-v14 precaches everything including the font) and the strict single-origin CSP lives in firebase.json rather than in any app's markup. The skins.mjs collision between signature-maker (264/0.022/warm/editorial/grain) and caregiver-log (250/0.035/warm/editorial/grain) is read straight from the file. HIGH CONFIDENCE, primary or multiply-corroborated sources: the DHS interim final rule 'Signatures on Immigration Benefit Requests', Federal Register document 2026-09289, published 11 May 2026, effective 10 July 2026, amending 8 CFR 103.2(a)(7)(ii)(A), with the fee-retention provision and the FY2021 300 to FY2025 2,953 denial figures reported consistently by Mintz, Ogletree, Erickson Immigration Group, Reddy Neumann Brown, NPZ and AILA; USCIS's signature definition and its rejection of typed, stamped and software-generated signatures (CitizenPath quoting USCIS, corroborated by Immigration Analytics); SignWell's verbatim privacy and no-account claims and its PNG/JPG export (fetched signwell.com/online-signature directly); Signaturely's verbatim privacy statement, its email-capture flow and its 'Sign 1 documents for free' footer CTA (fetched signaturely.com/online-signature directly); Online PNG Tools' verbatim client-side claim alongside its free-tier daily limits, wait timer, ads and premium-only clipboard (fetched directly); the Adobe Community blurry-Fill-and-Sign thread including the Community Expert reply about bit depth (fetched community.adobe.com thread 12364521 directly); Adobe's retirement of the standalone Fill & Sign app (helpx.adobe.com migration page, the page itself timed out on fetch but its title and summary were consistent across search results); szimek/signature_pad issue 254 verbatim (fetched GitHub directly); Section508.gov's electronic-signatures requirements (fetched directly); the Indian exam signature spec table and ranked rejection reasons including 'Format not JPEG, PNG is commonly rejected' (fetched examformtools.in directly); macOS Preview's trackpad, camera and iPhone signature capture (Apple Support guide prvw35725). MEDIUM CONFIDENCE: all pricing that came from third-party aggregators rather than the vendor's own page, SignWell paid tiers ($12 vs $15/user/mo differs between verdocs, costbench and research.com), Signaturely's free-plan limit (its own page says 1 document, several guides say 3, I have reported the contradiction rather than picking a side), Docusign Personal $15/mo with 5 envelopes and Standard $45 / Business Pro $60, Dropbox Sign free 3 requests and $15 to 25/user/mo, and Artlogo's $39 to 119+ range. Treat these as directional. Docusign's brand palette names (Cobalt, Inkwell, Deep Violet, Mist, Poppy) come from coverage of the 2024 rebrand and brand.docusign.com/color as indexed; I did not obtain hex values and have deliberately not invented any. LOW CONFIDENCE / EXPLICITLY FLAGGED: the app-store complaint entry. Both Google Play and the App Store render reviews with JavaScript; the one App Store page that did return content (id1491326276) showed only 6 ratings and two useless reviews, and the Play Store fetches truncated before the ratings, IAP prices, ads disclosure and Data Safety sections. Those complaints are paraphrases of aggregated search-result summaries, not verbatim quotes I read on a page, and I have said so in the source field rather than dressing them up. NOT AVAILABLE AT ALL, REDDIT: the WebSearch API refuses reddit.com outright in this environment ('domains are not accessible to our user agent'), DuckDuckGo Lite served a CAPTCHA on every attempt, and Bing's RSS endpoint ignored the site: operator and returned generic results. So there is zero first-hand forum sentiment in this document. That is the biggest hole: if you want the real gripe texture, someone should open r/legaladvice, r/sysadmin and r/pdf manually. Also unfetchable: serverless.tools and textstudio.com both returned 403, so their feature claims come from search-result summaries rather than the pages themselves; smallpngtools returned 409. Finally, one honest caveat on scope: the exam-portal workflow is enormous and well-evidenced but is predominantly an Indian-market use case, while SWS Strategic Media is a US LLC, I am confident the need is real and unserved by the well-designed tier, less confident it is the right first bet for this portfolio's audience. The USCIS finding, by contrast, is squarely US, squarely current, and squarely this app's problem.
